Migration to cucumber 3.0.0

Source: vignettes/migration-to-3-0-0.qmd

Cucumber 3.0.0 brings the package closer to the official Cucumber implementations: feature files are parsed by a port of the official Gherkin parser and step descriptions are Cucumber Expressions.

cucumber is tested against the test suites of the official Cucumber projects, see vignette("compatibility").

The checklist below finds and fixes everything that can break a project written for 2.2.0. The sections after it explain each change and why it was made. Where a change can break a project, a Migrating subsection shows what to change.

Migration checklist

Work through the steps in order. Run the searches from the project root. Each item links to its explanation.

1. Find what fails

  1. Upgrade cucumber to 3.0.0 and testthat to 3.3.2 or later.

  2. Run a dry run. It parses every feature file and matches every step to a step definition, without running any step or hook:

    cucumber::test(dry_run = TRUE)

    It reports every parse error with its file, line and column, every undefined step, every ambiguous step and every undefined parameter type. Fix them with the items below, and repeat until it reports none.

2. Rewrite what can be changed mechanically

These changes are safe without running the tests. The searches look in tests; use the directory of your feature files and step definitions.

Feature files. The dry run reports every parse error. See Feature files that were accepted and now fail, Steps with different text and Step arguments with different values.

Step definitions. See Migrating step descriptions.

  • Regular expression characters in a step description are now matched literally. Replace them with Cucumber Expressions, like apples? with apple(s):

    grep -rnE '(given|when|then)\("[^"]*[?*+|[]' tests

  • Escape a literal (, { or / in a description with \\(, \\{ or \\/.

  • Remove the ^ and $ of a description that uses a parameter like {int}, or write the whole description as a regular expression:

    grep -rnE '(given|when|then)\("\^.*\{' tests

  • Remove one of two step definitions that match the same step, like the {int} and float variants. Keep the float one.

Parameter types. See Migrating parameter types.

  • Replace four backslashes with two in define_parameter_type() regexps, like "\\\\d+" with "\\d+":

    grep -rnF '\\\\' tests

  • Rename a parameter type that redefines another one, like int, or is now built in: byte, short, long and double:

    grep -rnE 'define_parameter_type\("(int|float|word|string|byte|short|long|double)"' tests

  • Define every parameter type a description uses, or remove its braces.

Hooks. See Migrating hooks.

  • Replace the scenario_name argument with scenario and use scenario$name:

    grep -rn 'scenario_name' tests

Test runs. See Migrating test runs.

  • Write every tag expression, in test(), run() and hooks, with @ before tags and and, or and not in lowercase: "smoke AND NOT slow" becomes "@smoke and not @slow". Combine a vector of tag expressions with and, and a vector of filter regular expressions with |:

    grep -rnE '(tags|filter) *= *' tests

  • Remove the cucumber.indent option. It’s ignored:

    grep -rn 'cucumber.indent' .

  • Replace testthat reporters passed to test() or run() with cucumber’s: testthat::JunitReporter with CucumberJunitReporter, and others with CucumberSummaryReporter$new(), or NULL for no output:

    grep -rnE 'reporter *=|JunitReporter' tests

  • To see each step as it runs, as before, pass CucumberPrettyReporter$new(). Use it also where CucumberProgressReporter$new() gets reporter_max_docstring_lines or reporter_max_table_lines, and remove show_praise.

  • run() in a testthat file now reports nothing of its own. To print the run with cucumber’s reporter too, as before, pass reporter = CucumberProgressReporter$new().

  • Move the snapshots of _snaps/__cucumber__.md, or of the snapshot file of the test file that calls run(), to the snapshot file of each feature, like _snaps/basket.feature.md, or let the run save them again. See Snapshot files.

Custom reporters. See Migrating custom reporters.

grep -rnE 'start_feature|end_feature|start_step|end_step|start_reporter|end_reporter|start_test|end_test|add_result' R tests

3. Decide

These need a choice that depends on your project.

  • Pending and undefined steps fail their scenario. Implement them, or run with strict = FALSE to skip their scenarios. See Pending and undefined steps fail.

  • A Doc String is one string, not a character vector of lines. Where a step splits or indexes its doc_string, use strsplit(doc_string, "\n")[[1]], or set the cucumber.docstring_as_lines option to TRUE. See Feature files:

    grep -rn 'doc_string' tests

  • Capture groups in a parameter type’s regexp make its transformer get one argument per group. Make them non-capturing, (?:...), to keep the whole match, or give the transformer an argument per group. See Capture groups.

  • .feature files in subdirectories of the test directory now run. Move the ones that shouldn’t run, like test fixtures, out of it. See Feature files in subdirectories run.

  • Steps that relied on {int} matching +5, float needing a decimal point, or {word} matching only letters, digits and _. See Built-in parameter types.

4. Run the tests and review the differences

Run cucumber::test(). Failures that remain come from changes that only show in a run:

  • A failed expectation in a step, like expect_equal(), now fails the run. Before, its scenario was reported as skipped. See Failed expectations fail the run.

  • Steps that were silently dropped before now run, like a step indented deeper than the step above it. See Steps that were dropped and now run.

  • Doc Strings keep their comment and empty lines, escapes like \n in table cells are unescaped, and outline placeholders are replaced in step arguments. See Step arguments with different values.

  • Tags can contain # and :, and a description containing Feature: is no longer a second Feature. See Tags and descriptions.

  • Scenario names of outlines have no (Example n) suffix, and repeated names are numbered. Update the names you use in filter, name or when comparing test results. See Scenario names:

    grep -rn '(Example' tests

  • test() keeps the step definitions registered before it, and run() clears its own when it returns. See test() and run().

Feature files

Feature files are parsed by a port of the official Gherkin parser. For the official Gherkin test data, the package gives the same scenarios, steps, arguments and errors as the official parser.

A line’s meaning comes from the keyword it starts with, not from its indentation. Tabs, 4 spaces, no indentation and mixed indentation are all valid:

Feature: Basket
Scenario: Add an item
Given an empty basket

The parser also adds the following, all described in vignette("reference-gherkin"):

  • Rule with its own Background, 80 spoken languages with # language: and the cucumber.language option, and .feature.md files (Markdown with Gherkin).
  • Scenario Outline placeholders are replaced in names, Doc Strings and Data Tables. Examples can have a name and a description, and Examples: under a Scenario: makes it an outline.
  • A step can have both a Data Table and a Doc String. A Doc String is one string with its lines joined by "\n", and its media type is in the media_type attribute. The cucumber.docstring_as_lines option brings back the character vector of lines.
  • Ability: and Business Need: work as Feature:. An empty file, a file with only comments and a Feature: without scenarios run nothing instead of failing. A Scenario: without steps passes.
  • Every feature file is parsed before anything runs. If any can’t be parsed, no scenario runs and every error is reported with its file, line and column. Before, the files before the broken one ran and the rest were skipped.

Migrating feature files

Feature files that ran before can now fail to parse, and some steps get different text or arguments. Run cucumber::test() and fix the parse errors, then check the differences below.

The cucumber.indent option is removed: it’s ignored if set.

Feature files that were accepted and now fail

These were ignored without a warning, so their steps never ran. Now they fail with a parse error:

  • A line that isn’t a step, a table or a Doc String between steps.
  • A Background: after a Scenario:, or a second Background:.
  • A Doc String that isn’t closed before the end of the file.
  • A tag at the end of the file, with no Scenario:, Rule: or Examples: after it.
  • Two Doc Strings after one step. Before, they were merged into one Doc String.
  • A tag with whitespace, like @with space. Before, it was the tag @with.
  • # language: with an unknown language, like # language: xx, fails with Language not supported: xx. Before, the line was read as a comment.

Steps that were dropped and now run

  • A step indented deeper than the step above it. Before, Then b was dropped without a warning:

        Given a
      Then b

  • A step with a Doc String with a media type, or with both a Data Table and a Doc String. Before, the step got no argument.

  • Examples with a description, and Examples: under a Scenario:. Before, <x> wasn’t replaced.

Steps with different text

Line in a scenario Before Now
Given a<TAB>b step a (text cut at the tab) step a<TAB>b (only leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed)
Step one right after Scenario: step one description line, not a step (Step isn’t a Gherkin keyword)
Step one after a step step one parse error
Givenfoo after a step step foo parse error (a step keyword is followed by a space)
Given: x after a step step : x parse error
Given alone after a step step with empty text parse error
given b after a step dropped parse error (keywords are case-sensitive)

Step arguments with different values

Feature file Before Now
Doc String with an empty line and a line starting with # both lines dropped: "x <- 1" kept: "# comment\n\nx <- 1"
Doc String with \"\"\" inside say \"\"\" say """
Doc String whose """ is indented 4 spaces past its step 2 extra spaces on each line: c(" x", " y") dedented relative to the """: "x\n y"
Table cell a\nb a\nb (a backslash and n) a and b separated by a newline
Table cell a\\b a\\b a\b
Table header \| a \| \| columns a, V2 and a deprecation warning columns a and ""
Table header \| a \| a \| columns a, V2 columns a, a
Table rows \| foo \| bar \| / \| boz \| foo = "boz", bar = "boz" parse error: inconsistent cell count
Table rows \| a \| b \| / \| c \| d \| e \| e dropped with a warning parse error: inconsistent cell count
Table rows \| a \| b \| / \| c \| d table dropped parse error: inconsistent cell count
Table row \| a \| b \| note table dropped note is ignored, the table has columns a and b
Outline step argument with <x> <x> the Examples value

Scenario names

  • Scenario names are the outline name with placeholders replaced, without an (Example n) suffix. Scenario Outline: eat <n> with two Examples tables runs eat 1 and eat 2. Before, it ran eat <n> (Example 1) twice, because the counter restarted in each Examples table.
  • Scenarios that share a name, like the rows of an outline without placeholders in its name, are numbered in test results: eating (1), eating (2). testthat merges the results of tests with the same name, so before, results of repeated names were lost.

If you filter scenarios by name, or compare test results by name, update the names you use.

Tags and descriptions

  • Tags are everything up to whitespace: @a#2 @a:b are the tags @a#2 and @a:b. Before, both were the tag @a. Text after # on a tag line is a comment.
  • Feature: in a description line, like A Feature: in the description., no longer counts as a second Feature.

Step descriptions

Step descriptions support the full Cucumber Expressions syntax:

# Optional text: matches "1 cucumber" and "2 cucumbers"
given("I have {int} cucumber(s)", function(n, context) { ... })

# Alternative words: matches "I press Enter" and "I press Return"
when("I press Enter/Return", function(context) { ... })

# Escaped space keeps words together: matches "I live in New York" and "I live in Boston"
given("I live in New\\ York/Boston", function(context) { ... })

# Anonymous parameter: matches anything and passes it as text
given("I am {}", function(who, context) { ... })

A description that starts with ^, ends with $ or is surrounded by / is a regular expression, as in cucumber-jvm. Each capture group’s text is passed to the step, NA if the group didn’t match. A group whose regexp is a parameter type’s regexp, like (\d+) for {int}, is transformed by that parameter type:

# n is an integer
given("^I have (\\d+) cucumbers$", function(n, context) { ... })

Invalid Cucumber Expressions are an error that points at the problem: an empty optional (), an optional inside an optional, a parameter inside an optional, an alternation inside an optional, an empty alternative (/about, a//b, {int}/{int}), an alternative made of optionals only, a missing ) or }, an illegal character in a parameter name, and escaping a character that can’t be escaped. When the message suggests an escape, it also shows how to write it in an R string.

A step that matches more than one step definition fails with an error listing every matching definition and where it’s defined.

Migrating step descriptions

Text is matched literally

Text in step descriptions was treated as a regular expression, so characters like ., ?, *, | or [ could change what a step matched. Now it’s matched literally. Use Cucumber Expressions instead:

# Before: matched "I have 3 apples" and "I have 3 apple"
given("I have {int} apples?", function(n, context) { ... })

# Now
given("I have {int} apple(s)", function(n, context) { ... })

(, { and / have a meaning in Cucumber Expressions. To match them literally, escape them with \\(, \\{ or \\/:

given("I visit \\/about", function(context) { ... })

Descriptions with ^ or $

Before, a description starting with ^ or ending with $ was a Cucumber Expression. Now it’s a regular expression, so its parameters like {int} don’t work. Remove the anchors, or write it as a regular expression:

# Before
given("^I have {int} cucumbers$", function(n, context) { ... })

# Now
given("I have {int} cucumbers", function(n, context) { ... })

Undefined parameter types

A step definition that uses a parameter type that isn’t defined, like {colour} without define_parameter_type("colour", ...), defines no step. The steps it would match are undefined, and the summary of the run lists the undefined parameter types. Define it, or remove the braces.

Ambiguous steps

Before, when a step matched more than one step definition, the first registered one was used without a warning, unless the definitions were identical. Now the step fails. Remove the duplicates.

A common case is defining a step for both {int} and float. float now matches integers too, so keep only the float one:

# Before
given("I pay {int} dollars", function(amount, context) { ... })
given("I pay {float} dollars", function(amount, context) { ... })

# Now
given("I pay {float} dollars", function(amount, context) { ... })

Use cucumber::test(dry_run = TRUE) to find every ambiguous and undefined step without running any steps.

Step definitions

Cleanup with context

Code a step or a hook defers in its context runs when the scenario ends, after its after() hooks, like code deferred in a testthat test. Without context, it’s undone when the step ends:

given("the shop is closed", function(context) {
  withr::local_options(shop.open = FALSE, .local_envir = context)
  testthat::local_mocked_bindings(now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 22:00"), .env = context)
})

An error of the deferred code is a warning of the scenario, Cleanup of the scenario failed, as its steps already have their results.

Errors

  • An error in a step is shown with its backtrace, the calls of the step down to where it was thrown, like an error in a testthat test. Cucumber’s reporters print it under the step’s error, testthat’s reporters show it under run(), and Cucumber Messages have it as the exception’s stackTrace.
  • The error of a step or a hook names its feature file with a line, like Feature: checkout/basket.feature:3, so IDEs can open it there: the step’s line for a step, the scenario’s line for a hook.
  • A step definition with the wrong number of arguments fails the step with an error that says how many arguments the step passes and the function to use, e.g. Use `function(int, data_table, context)`. Before, it failed with unused argument. A step definition with ... gets the step’s arguments by position.
  • Defining a step without context as its last argument is an error that shows the function to use, e.g. Use `function(n, context)`, or suggests renaming a misnamed last argument: Use `function(n, ctx, context)`, or rename `ctx` to `context`. Before, it was a checkmate error, Must be a subset of {'n'}.
  • When no step definitions are loaded, an undefined step says to define them in setup-*.R or helper-*.R files of the test directory, as other R files there aren’t run.

Parameter types

Built-in parameter types match the same values as in Cucumber Expressions:

Parameter Matches
{int} -?\d+. A value out of R’s integer range fails the step
float integers like 12, decimals like -1.5 and .5, and exponents like 1.5E3
{word} anything without whitespace, like foo-bar or a.b
{string} text in quotes, with escaped quotes: "say \"hi\"" passes say "hi"
{byte}, {short} like {int}
{long} like {int}, but gives a double, as a long can be too big for an R integer
{double} like float

{byte}, {short}, {long} and {double} aren’t used in snippets.

define_parameter_type() accepts several regexps, and gets the use_for_snippets and prefer_for_regexp_match options. Its transformer is optional: without one, the step gets the text as it is.

define_parameter_type() fails on an empty name, as {} is the anonymous parameter type, and on an invalid regexp, with an error that names the parameter type and says why, like The regexp /(green/ of parameter type {colour} is invalid. Before, an invalid regexp failed the steps that used it, with an error of stri_detect_regex().

An error of a transformer fails the step with Parameter type {colour} failed to transform "blue"., caused by the transformer’s error, and its backtrace is the calls of the transformer.

If a parameter type’s regexp has capture groups, its transformer gets the text of each group as a separate argument, like in Cucumber:

define_parameter_type("point", "(\\d+),(\\d+)", function(x, y) c(as.integer(x), as.integer(y)))

given("the point {point}", function(point, context) { ... })

Migrating parameter types

Built-in parameter types

Parameter Before Now
{int} +5 matched, a value out of R’s integer range became NA +5 doesn’t match, a value out of R’s integer range fails the step
float needed a decimal point, which matched any character integers match too, the decimal point must be .
{word} letters, digits and _ anything without whitespace

If you defined a step for both {int} and float, see Ambiguous steps.

Regexps are used as is

Before, a parameter type’s regexp was a replacement string, so special characters needed four backslashes:

# Before
define_parameter_type("sci_number", "[+-]?\\\\d*\\\\.?\\\\d+", as.double)

# Now
define_parameter_type("sci_number", "[+-]?\\d*\\.?\\d+", as.double)

Capture groups

Before, a transformer got the whole match, and capture groups made later parameters of the step get wrong values. To keep passing the whole match, use non-capturing groups, (?:...):

# Before
define_parameter_type("colour", "(dark )?(red|blue)", as.character)

# Now
define_parameter_type("colour", "(?:dark )?(?:red|blue)", as.character)

Parameter types can’t be redefined

define_parameter_type() fails on a name that is already defined differently, like int. Defining the same parameter type again, like when a setup file is loaded twice, replaces it. Before, the second definition silently replaced the first. Give your parameter type its own name, e.g. {count}. A name can’t contain {, }, (, ), \ or /, and only one parameter type with the same regexp can have prefer_for_regexp_match = TRUE.

{byte}, {short}, {long} and {double} are built in now, so a parameter type of your own with one of these names must be renamed. A regular expression group whose regexp is float’s is ambiguous between float and {double}.

Running tests

Every step gets a result: passed, failed, pending, undefined, ambiguous or skipped. Steps after a step that didn’t pass are reported as skipped.

Undefined and ambiguous steps don’t stop the run. They fail their scenario, and the other scenarios and feature files still run, so every missing step’s snippet is shown.

test() and run() search path recursively for feature files, symbolic links included.

test() and run() get new arguments:

# Match every step to a step definition, without running steps or hooks
cucumber::test(dry_run = TRUE)

# Run scenarios whose name matches a regular expression
cucumber::test(name = "^Adding")

# Run the scenario at line 12 of a feature file, or the feature files of a directory
cucumber::test(features = c("addition.feature:12", "checkout"))

# Skip the remaining scenarios after the first failed one
cucumber::test(fail_fast = TRUE)

# Run a failed scenario again, up to 2 more times
cucumber::test(retry = 2)

# Run the scenarios in reverse or random order
cucumber::test(order = "random")
  • A dry run reports undefined and ambiguous steps, but they don’t fail it: their scenarios are skipped.
  • The line of a Scenario Outline in features runs all its examples, the line of an example row runs only that example. An empty features, like a rerun file of a run whose scenarios passed, runs no scenario, and empty strings in it are ignored.
  • With fail_fast, the remaining scenarios are skipped and their hooks don’t run. With strict = TRUE, a scenario with a pending or undefined step counts as failed.
  • With retry, the last attempt of a scenario is its result. Pending, undefined and ambiguous scenarios aren’t retried. Each attempt is reported, with (attempt 2) after the scenario’s name, the summary counts only the last attempt, and testthat gets the expectations of only the last attempt.
  • A random order shows its seed, and order = "random:<seed>" runs the scenarios in that order again.

test() called without path runs the feature files of the directory in the cucumber.path option, "tests/acceptance" by default:

options(cucumber.path = "features")

test() and run()

  • test() runs feature files like testthat::test_dir() runs test files: in path, after the helper-*.R and setup-*.R files and before the teardown-*.R files. Each feature file is the file of its scenarios’ results. Before, test() wrote a test-__cucumber__.R file into path, which failed in a read-only directory.
  • test() attaches cucumber, so setup files define steps without cucumber::. Before, they failed with could not find function "given".
  • test() checks snapshots when NOT_CRAN isn’t set, like testthat::test_local(). testthat::testing_package() is the package of path, so local_mocked_bindings(.env = context) mocks its functions without .package.
  • test() keeps the step definitions, hooks and parameter types registered before it. Before, it cleared them.
  • test() fails with the error that stopped the run, like an unparsable feature file, under Test failures., even with reporter = NULL.
  • run() works outside of a testthat run: it attaches testthat, reports with CucumberProgressReporter, fails with Test failures. if a scenario failed, and clears its step definitions and hooks when it returns. Before, it failed with “teardown_env() has not been initialized”.
  • test(), run() and features_rd() check their arguments before anything runs and name the wrong one, like `dry_run` must be `TRUE` or `FALSE`.
  • test() passes its ... to grepl() when matching filter, e.g. test(filter = "ADDITION", ignore.case = TRUE). An argument of neither, like a misspelled fail_fst = TRUE, is an error.
  • A test_that() test after run() in a test file is reported in the test file’s context.

Snapshots

Each feature file has a snapshot file of its own in _snaps, like _snaps/basket.feature.md or, for checkout/basket.feature, _snaps/checkout-basket.feature.md. test() and run() use the same files. expect_snapshot() works in steps and in scenario and step hooks. A snapshot is named after its scenario. Snapshots of scenarios that didn’t run are kept, and those of renamed or removed scenarios are deleted. vignette("testthat") has the details. cucumber needs testthat 3.3.2 or later.

Migrating test runs

Feature files in subdirectories run

Before, only the files directly in path ran, and the others were ignored. Move .feature files that shouldn’t run, like test fixtures, out of path.

Pending and undefined steps fail

Before, pending() skipped the scenario, and an undefined step stopped the run. Now both fail the scenario. To skip these scenarios instead, run with strict = FALSE:

cucumber::test("tests/acceptance", strict = FALSE)

A run without any step definitions reports its steps as undefined, instead of failing with “No step definitions found”.

Tag expressions

Tag expressions are parsed like the official cucumber/tag-expressions. Write tags with their @, and and, or and not in lowercase:

# Before
cucumber::test(tags = "smoke AND NOT slow")

# Now
cucumber::test(tags = "@smoke and not @slow")

A tag is everything up to whitespace or a parenthesis, so tags with :, / or # work. Escape a parenthesis in a tag with a backslash: tags = "@wip\\(x\\)".

tags must be one tag expression, and filter one regular expression. Before, only the first of several was used. Combine them:

# Before
cucumber::test(tags = c("@smoke", "not @slow"), filter = c("basket", "checkout"))

# Now
cucumber::test(tags = "@smoke and not @slow", filter = "basket|checkout")

An invalid tag expression fails with the official error, e.g. Tag expression "@a @b" could not be parsed because of syntax error: Expected operator., before anything runs, even with stop_on_failure = FALSE.

Snapshot files

test() saved snapshots in _snaps/__cucumber__.md, and run() in the snapshot file of the testthat file that called it, like _snaps/acceptance.md. Move each scenario’s snapshots to the snapshot file of its feature, see Snapshots, before you run the tests, or let the run save them again. A run of every scenario deletes the old snapshot files as unused: testthat deletes _snaps/acceptance.md as the snapshot file of a test file without snapshots, and cucumber deletes _snaps/__cucumber__.md.

Failed expectations fail the run

Before, a failed expectation in a step, like expect_equal(), wasn’t recorded by testthat, so the scenario was reported as skipped. Now it fails the run, so tests that seemed to pass may fail. Its message is like the error of a step: Step "<text>" failed, the scenario’s feature and name, and where the step is defined, then the expectation’s message.

Other results that were wrong before:

  • A step or a hook fails when a test_that() test in it fails, with The test "<name>" in the step failed. Before, the step and its scenario passed, while testthat reported the test in it as failed.
  • A scenario whose steps pass without calling any expect_*() function is reported as passed. Before, testthat reported it as skipped (“empty test”).
  • testthat’s reporters show a step’s error like an error in a test, starting with Error: Step "<text>" failed. Before, it started with the error’s classes, <cucumber_step_error/rlang_error/error/condition>.

Hooks

  • before() and after() hooks get the scenario: a list with its name, tags, uri, line and id, and in after() hooks its status and error. The line of an example of a Scenario Outline is the line of its row. The status is the worst result of the scenario’s steps and of the hooks that ran before it.
  • Define any number of hooks of each kind. Before hooks run in the order they are defined, after hooks in the reverse order.
  • Hooks get a tags argument, a tag expression. The hook runs only for scenarios that match it.
  • Hooks get a name argument. A named hook’s errors start with its name, e.g. Hook "Connect to the database" failed.
  • before_step() and after_step() hooks run around each step. They get the step’s keyword, text, line, and its data_table and doc_string as its step definition gets them, and in after_step() its status and error. A failing step hook fails the step.
  • before_all() and after_all() hooks run once before the first and after the last scenario of a run. They get no arguments, or a context to attach data to the report. Every before_all() hook runs even when one of them fails: then no scenario runs, and the run fails with the first error.
  • A before() hook skips its scenario by calling skip_scenario(). The rest of the before hooks and the scenario’s steps are skipped, and after() hooks get "skipped" as the scenario’s status. A step can call skip_scenario() too: it and the steps after it are skipped, and after() hooks still run.
  • skip() or skip_scenario() in a before_all() hook skips every scenario of the run, like skip() at the top of a testthat file, e.g. before_all(function() skip_if_offline()). In an after() hook, it skips that hook: the next after() hooks still run, and the scenario is reported as skipped if it didn’t fail.
  • A failing before() hook reports the scenario’s steps as skipped and fails the scenario.
  • A failing hook’s error says which hook failed, like Hook `before()` failed, or its name, the scenario’s feature and name, and where the hook is defined. after() hooks get it as scenario$error, with the hook’s own error as its parent.
  • A printed scenario shows its name and where it is, like <scenario> "Add an item" (basket.feature:2). A printed context lists what steps and hooks put in it, one line each, and its methods. Like a tibble, it shows the first 10 items; print(context, n = 20) shows more.
before(function(context, scenario) {
  context$db <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
}, tags = "@db", name = "Connect to the database")

before(function(context, scenario) {
  if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("API_KEY"))) skip_scenario("API_KEY is not set")
}, tags = "@api")

after(function(context, scenario) {
  if (scenario$status == "failed") message(scenario$name, " failed")
})

after_step(function(context, step) {
  message(step$text, ": ", step$status)
})

Migrating hooks

A hook’s second argument is the scenario instead of its name. Replace scenario_name with scenario$name:

# Before
after(function(context, scenario_name) {
  message("Finished ", scenario_name)
})

# Now
after(function(context, scenario) {
  message("Finished ", scenario$name)
})

Before, a second hook of the same kind failed with “Hook already registered”.

Reporters

  • The default reporter, CucumberProgressReporter, prints one line per feature with its scenarios counted by status, like testthat’s ProgressReporter, redrawn with a spinner while the feature runs. A scenario that didn’t pass is printed as soon as it finishes, and again in the summary. The reporter that printed each step is now CucumberPrettyReporter, like Cucumber’s pretty formatter.
  • run() in a testthat file reports nothing of its own by default: testthat’s reporter reports each scenario as a test, and a failed expectation names its step, like Step "the result is 2" failed. Pass a reporter to run() to print the run with cucumber’s reporter too.
  • testthat’s reporters show a scenario’s failure, skip or warning at its line of the feature file, like Failure ('basket.feature:4:1'): the line of the step, or of the scenario for a hook. Before, they showed the line of the test file that called run().
  • Cucumber reporters aren’t testthat reporters anymore, and testthat reporters can’t report a cucumber run. A CucumberReporter gets the start and the end of the run, start_run() and end_run(error), its warnings, add_warning(), and the run as Cucumber Messages, add_message(): each feature, scenario, step and hook, and their results. Use reporter = NULL to report nothing.
  • CucumberPrettyReporter prints each step with the keyword it’s written with, its Doc String and Data Table as written, each scenario with its keyword, like Example: or Scenario Outline:, the Rule: before its first scenario, a step’s warnings under the step, and a failed hook’s error where it happens. It summarises the run like Cucumber, counting scenarios and steps by status, e.g. 2 scenarios (1 failed, 1 passed). Before, a step’s warnings were printed above it.
  • An error of a reporter stops the run with an error that names the reporter and the event, like Reporter `MyReporter` failed in `add_message()`., even with stop_on_failure = FALSE. Before, testthat reported it as the failure of the scenario.

New reporters, like the formatters of Cucumber:

Reporter Like Cucumber’s Reports
CucumberDotsReporter progress one character per step and hook: . passed, F failed, - skipped, P pending, U undefined, A ambiguous
CucumberProgressBarReporter progress-bar a bar of the steps run so far, and each scenario that didn’t pass
CucumberSummaryReporter summary the failures, the warnings, the counts by status and how long the run took
CucumberRerunReporter rerun where the scenarios that didn’t pass are, like basket.feature:5:14, to pass to features
CucumberUsageReporter usage how each step definition was used, the slowest steps first, and unused step definitions
CucumberSnippetsReporter snippets only the snippets of undefined steps, one per step
CucumberMessagesReporter message the run as Cucumber Messages, one JSON message per line
CucumberHtmlReporter html the official Cucumber HTML report
CucumberJunitReporter junit the JUnit XML report, for CI services
CucumberMultiReporter passes every event to each of its reporters

The reporters that print, print to a file instead when given one, e.g. CucumberSummaryReporter$new(file = "summary.txt"). The reporters that write a file create its directory. report(file) of every reporter reports a run after it ran, from the messages a CucumberMessagesReporter stored:

cucumber::test(reporter = CucumberMultiReporter$new(list(
  CucumberProgressReporter$new(),
  CucumberMessagesReporter$new("cucumber.ndjson")
)))
CucumberHtmlReporter$new("report.html")$report("cucumber.ndjson")

Migrating custom reporters

This matters only for custom reporters. start_feature(), end_feature(), start_step() and end_step() are removed: read the run from the messages in add_message() instead. A step’s result is in its testStepFinished message, whose testStepId is the id of a test step of the scenario’s testCase. That test step’s pickleStepId is the id of a step of the scenario’s pickle, with the step’s text.

# Before
StatusReporter <- R6::R6Class(
  "StatusReporter",
  inherit = cucumber::CucumberReporter,
  public = list(
    end_step = function(step) message(step$text, ": ", step$status)
  )
)

# Now
StatusReporter <- R6::R6Class(
  "StatusReporter",
  inherit = cucumber::CucumberReporter,
  public = list(
    add_message = function(envelope) {
      finished <- envelope$testStepFinished
      if (!is.null(finished)) message(finished$testStepId, ": ", finished$testStepResult$status)
    }
  )
)

A step’s status is "FAILED" for both failed expectations and errors. The "error" status is removed.

show_praise of CucumberPrettyReporter$new() is deprecated and warns, as it never had an effect.

Reports

  • read_messages() reads the Cucumber Messages of a run as tibbles of its features, scenarios and steps and hooks, with their status, duration and error, to write a report of your own. A retried scenario has the steps of its last attempt, and its attempts column tells how many it took.
  • Steps and hooks attach data to the report with their context: context$attach(data, media_type, file_name) attaches a string or a raw vector, like a screenshot, context$log(text) attaches text and context$link(url) a link. The HTML report shows them, and CucumberPrettyReporter prints logs and links under their step.

See vignette("reporting") for how to write the HTML report of a run, attach a screenshot of a failing shinytest2 scenario to it, and keep the report of a CI run.

Features as documentation

features_rd() puts scenarios of feature files in the help page of a function, in a section named "Behavior" by default:

#' @eval cucumber::features_rd(features = "basket.feature")

It selects scenarios like test(), by features, filter, name and tags. By default only scenarios tagged "@rd" are selected. The cucumber.rd_tags option sets another tag expression, and section or the cucumber.rd_section option names the section. Each feature is shown as one block of Gherkin, with only the Rules, Backgrounds and Examples of the selected scenarios. On a pkgdown site it’s shown like Markdown with Gherkin, and markdown = FALSE keeps the block of Gherkin. See vignette("bdd").

Snippets

Snippets for undefined steps are generated like in Cucumber. A value matched by several parameter types gives one suggestion per type, like {int} and a commented-out float for 5. Custom parameter types are used, (, { and / are escaped, and a step with a Data Table or Doc String gets a data_table or doc_string argument. A step starting with And, But or * gets given(), when() or then() from its type. A step that starts with ^ or ends with $ gets a regular expression, like when("^I pay 5\\$$", ...).
